title: Gun Control
question: What should the laws say about who may have a gun?
summary: A calm page about gun laws. It will include strong evidence used by both sides, stay age-appropriate, and skip graphic stories.
sourceNote: Further reading only. This outline does not take facts from these pages yet. When the full page is written, government or other primary sources will be cited first, and the Just Facts page will stay linked as further reading. The wording on this site will stay original. No statistics are included here.

paragraphs: This section will explain, without graphic detail, what people are arguing about: which guns are legal, who may buy one, where a gun may be carried, and what the Constitution has to do with it. Violent incidents will not be described.
No statistics will be added until they are checked against primary sources.

This section will give the strongest fair case for tighter laws and the strongest fair case for keeping lawful ownership broad. It will look for solid research on both sides, including research that a single source might leave out. It will not treat a chart as proof of a cause unless the evidence really shows a cause.

sides.intro: Each column will hold one side’s strongest fair case, in plain language and at similar length. Neither case is written yet.

a.title: One side’s strongest case
paragraphs: This column will give the strongest fair case for one view, using checked facts. It will not use insults, and it is not written yet.

b.title: The other side’s strongest case
paragraphs: This column will give the strongest fair case for the other view, under the same rules. It is not written yet.
This section will look for aims people share even when they disagree about the law, such as wanting fewer people hurt and wanting the rules to apply fairly.

items: The questions will ask how a right and a risk can both be real, what evidence would change a person’s mind, and how to talk about this without using fear in place of facts.

sources.title: Bureau of Justice Statistics
sources.note: A federal justice-statistics agency. The full page will also check public-health research and will not rely on one organization’s choice of facts. No injury or crime figures are included here.

sources.title: Just Facts: Gun Control
